sanskrit: hriyamāṇā tu vaidehī kaṃ cin nātham apaśyatī dadarśa giriśṛṅgasthān pañcavānarapuṃgavān
english: As Vaidehī was being carried off, seeing no protector anywhere, she beheld five foremost monkeys stationed on a mountain peak.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ madhye viśālākṣī kauśeyaṃ kanakaprabham uttarīyaṃ varārohā śubhāny ābharaṇāni ca mumoca yadi rāmāya śaṃseyur iti maithilī
english: The wide-eyed Maithilī, of beautiful form, dropped among them her upper garment of silk, bright as gold, and her auspicious ornaments — thinking they might report to Rāma.

sanskrit: vastram utsṛjya tan madhye vinikṣiptaṃ sabhūṣaṇam saṃbhramāt tu daśagrīvas tat karma na ca buddhivān
english: She cast down that garment together with the ornaments into their midst; but Daśagrīva, bewildered and dull of wit, did not perceive her act.

sanskrit: piṅgākṣās tāṃ viśālākṣīṃ netrair animiṣair iva vikrośantīṃ tadā sītāṃ dadṛśur vānararṣabhāḥ
english: The tawny-eyed bull-monkeys gazed with unblinking eyes at wide-eyed Sītā as she cried out pitifully.

sanskrit: sa ca pampām atikramya laṅkām abhimukhaḥ purīm jagāma rudatīṃ gṛhya maithilīṃ rākṣaseśvaraḥ
english: Crossing beyond the Pampā lake, the lord of rākṣasas went, holding weeping Maithilī, with his face turned toward the city of Laṅkā.

sanskrit: tāṃ jahāra susaṃhṛṣṭo rāvaṇo mṛtyum ātmanaḥ utsaṅgeneva bhujagīṃ tīkṣṇadaṃṣṭrāṃ mahāviṣām
english: Rāvaṇa, greatly exultant, seized her — his own death — even as one clasps in one's lap a sharp-fanged serpent of great venom.

sanskrit: vanāni saritaḥ śailān sarāṃsi ca vihāyasā sa kṣipraṃ samatīyāya śaraś cāpād iva cyutaḥ
english: Swiftly he traversed through the sky forests, rivers, mountains, and lakes, like an arrow released from a bow.

sanskrit: timinakraniketaṃ tu varuṇālayam akṣayam saritāṃ śaraṇaṃ gatvā samatīyāya sāgaram
english: He came to the ocean — the home of Varuṇa, inexhaustible, the abode of timi-fish and crocodiles, the refuge of rivers — and crossed it.

sanskrit: saṃbhramāt parivṛttormī ruddhamīnamahoragaḥ vaidehyāṃ hriyamāṇāyāṃ babhūva varuṇālayaḥ
english: As Vaidehī was being carried off, the ocean — Varuṇa's domain — became agitated with turbulent waves, its fish and great serpents restrained.

sanskrit: antarikṣagatā vācaḥ sasṛjuś cāraṇās tadā etad anto daśagrīva iti siddhās tadābruvan
english: Then the Cāraṇas moving through the sky called out; the Siddhas too declared at that moment: "This, O Daśagrīva, is your end."

sanskrit: sa tu sītāṃ viveṣṭantīm aṅkenādāya rāvaṇaḥ praviveśa purīṃ laṅkāṃ rūpiṇīṃ mṛtyum ātmanaḥ
english: Taking on his lap Sītā as she writhed and struggled, Rāvaṇa entered the city of Laṅkā — his own death incarnate.

sanskrit: so 'bhigamya purīṃ laṅkāṃ suvibhaktamahāpathām saṃrūḍhakakṣyā bahulaṃ svam antaḥpuram āviśat
english: Reaching the city of Laṅkā with its great roads well laid out, he entered his own inner apartments, richly furnished with fully grown enclosures.

sanskrit: tatra tām asitāpāṅgīṃ śokamohaparāyaṇām nidadhe rāvaṇaḥ sītāṃ mayo māyām ivāsurīm
english: There Rāvaṇa placed dark-eyed Sītā, wholly overcome with grief and stupor, as Maya placed his demonic māyā.

sanskrit: abravīc ca daśagrīvaḥ piśācīr ghoradarśanāḥ yathā naināṃ pumān strī vā sītāṃ paśyaty asaṃmataḥ
english: Daśagrīva then spoke to the dreadful-looking demonesses: let no man or woman look upon Sītā without his sanction.

sanskrit: muktāmaṇisuvarṇāni vastrāṇy ābharaṇāni ca yad yad icchet tad evāsyā deyaṃ macchandato yathā
english: "Whatever she desires — pearls, gems, gold, garments, ornaments — all that shall be given to her in accordance with my wish."

sanskrit: yā ca vakṣyati vaidehīṃ vacanaṃ kiṃ cid apriyam ajñānād yadi vā jñānān na tasyā jīvitaṃ priyam
english: "And she who speaks any unpleasant word to Vaidehī, whether from ignorance or knowingly — her life shall be forfeit."

sanskrit: tathoktvā rākṣasīs tās tu rākṣasendraḥ pratāpavān niṣkramyāntaḥpurāt tasmāt kiṃ kṛtyam iti cintayan dadarśāṣṭau mahāvīryān rākṣasān piśitāśanān
english: Having spoken thus to those demonesses, the powerful lord of rākṣasas departed from the inner apartments and, pondering what was to be done, he beheld eight mighty flesh-eating rākṣasas.

sanskrit: sa tān dṛṣṭvā mahāvīryo varadānena mohitaḥ uvācaitān idaṃ vākyaṃ praśasya balavīryataḥ
english: That most mighty one, intoxicated by boons granted to him, beholding them, praised their strength and valor and spoke these words to them.

sanskrit: nānāpraharaṇāḥ kṣipram ito gacchata satvarāḥ janasthānaṃ hatasthānaṃ bhūtapūrvaṃ kharālayam
english: "Armed with various weapons, go from here swiftly and quickly to Janasthāna, the ruined place, the former abode of Khara."

sanskrit: tatroṣyatāṃ janasthāne śūnye nihatarākṣase pauruṣaṃ balam āśritya trāsam utsṛjya dūrataḥ
english: "Stay there in Janasthāna, now empty with its rākṣasas slain, relying on your manly valor, casting fear far away."

sanskrit: balaṃ hi sumahad yan me janasthāne niveśitam sadūṣaṇakharaṃ yuddhe hataṃ tad rāmasāyakaiḥ
english: "For the great force I had stationed in Janasthāna — along with Dūṣaṇa and Khara — has been slain in battle by Rāma's arrows."

sanskrit: tataḥ krodho mamāpūrvo dhairyasyopari vardhate vairaṃ ca sumahaj jātaṃ rāmaṃ prati sudāruṇam
english: "Hence an unprecedented rage mounts over my composure, and a great, dreadful enmity toward Rāma has arisen within me."

sanskrit: niryātayitum icchāmi tac ca vairam ahaṃ ripoḥ na hi lapsyāmy ahaṃ nidrām ahatvā saṃyuge ripum
english: "I wish to repay that enmity to my enemy; truly I shall not find sleep without slaying my foe in battle."

sanskrit: taṃ tv idānīm ahaṃ hatvā kharadūṣaṇaghātinam rāmaṃ śarmopalapsyāmi dhanaṃ labdhveva nirdhanaḥ
english: "Slaying him now — Rāma the killer of Khara and Dūṣaṇa — I shall attain peace, as a pauper attains ease upon gaining wealth."

sanskrit: janasthāne vasadbhis tu bhavadbhī rāmam āśritā pravṛttir upanetavyā kiṃ karotīti tattvataḥ
english: "While dwelling in Janasthāna, you must bring me true intelligence of all that concerns Rāma — what he is doing and how."

sanskrit: apramādāc ca gantavyaṃ sarvair eva niśācaraiḥ kartavyaś ca sadā yatno rāghavasya vadhaṃ prati
english: "All night-wanderers must go there without carelessness, and effort must ever be made toward the slaying of Rāghava."

sanskrit: yuṣmākaṃ hi balajño 'haṃ bahuśo raṇamūrdhani ataś cāsmiñ janasthāne mayā yūyaṃ niyojitāḥ
english: "For I know your strength well from many a battle-front; and it is for that reason I have assigned you to this Janasthāna."

sanskrit: tataḥ priyaṃ vākyam upetya rākṣasā mahārtham aṣṭāv abhivādya rāvaṇam vihāya laṅkāṃ sahitāḥ pratasthire yato janasthānam alakṣyadarśanāḥ
english: Then those eight rākṣasas, receiving these pleasing and weighty words, saluted Rāvaṇa and together departed from Laṅkā toward Janasthāna, vanishing from sight.

sanskrit: tatas tu sītām upalabhya rāvaṇaḥ susaṃprahṛṣṭaḥ parigṛhya maithilīm prasajya rāmeṇa ca vairam uttamaṃ babhūva mohān muditaḥ sa rākṣasaḥ
english: Having thus secured Sītā and taken possession of Maithilī, Rāvaṇa was greatly exultant; and having now committed himself to supreme enmity with Rāma, that rākṣasa was delighted through his own delusion.

sanskrit: saṃdiśya rākṣasān ghorān rāvaṇo 'ṣṭau mahābalān ātmānaṃ buddhivaiklavyāt kṛtakṛtyam amanyata
english: Having dispatched the eight terrible, mighty rākṣasas, Rāvaṇa, through the confusion of his intellect, considered himself as having accomplished his purpose.

sanskrit: sa cintayāno vaidehīṃ kāmabāṇasamarpitaḥ praviveśa gṛhaṃ ramyaṃ sītāṃ draṣṭum abhitvaran
english: Thinking of Vaidehī, pierced through by the arrows of love, he hastily entered his beautiful dwelling, eager to see Sītā.

sanskrit: sa praviśya tu tadveśma rāvaṇo rākṣasādhipaḥ apaśyad rākṣasīmadhye sītāṃ śokaparāyaṇam
english: Rāvaṇa, the lord of rākṣasas, entering that dwelling, saw Sītā in the midst of the demonesses, wholly given over to grief.

sanskrit: aśrupūrṇamukhīṃ dīnāṃ śokabhārāvapīḍitām vāyuvegair ivākrāntāṃ majjantīṃ nāvam arṇave
english: Her face filled with tears, wretched, crushed by the weight of sorrow, like a boat assailed by fierce winds sinking in the ocean.

sanskrit: mṛgayūthaparibhraṣṭāṃ mṛgīṃ śvabhir ivāvṛtām adhomukhamukhīṃ dīnām abhyetya ca niśācaraḥ
english: Strayed from her herd of deer, like a doe surrounded by dogs, her face cast downward, wretched — the night-stalker approached her.

sanskrit: tāṃ tu śokavaśāṃ dīnām avaśāṃ rākṣasādhipaḥ sa balād darśayām āsa gṛhaṃ devagṛhopamam
english: The lord of rākṣasas then forcefully showed that wretched, helpless one, overcome by grief, his palace comparable to the abode of the gods.

sanskrit: harmyaprāsādasaṃbadhaṃ strīsahasraniṣevitam nānāpakṣigaṇair juṣṭaṃ nānāratnasamanvitam
english: It was filled with mansions and palaces, frequented by thousands of women, thronged with diverse flocks of birds, adorned with gems of every kind.

sanskrit: kāñcanais tāpanīyaiś ca sphāṭikai rājatais tathā vajravaidūryacitraiś ca stambhair dṛṣṭimanoharaiḥ
english: With pillars of gold and refined gold, of crystal and silver, inlaid with diamond and vaidūrya, captivating to the eye.

sanskrit: divyadundubhinirhrādaṃ taptakāñcanatoraṇam sopānaṃ kāñcanaṃ citram āruroha tayā saha
english: Resounding with divine kettledrums, with archways of refined gold, he ascended with her the splendid golden stairway.

sanskrit: dāntakā rājatāś caiva gavākṣāḥ priyadarśanāḥ hemajālāvṛtāś cāsaṃs tatra prāsādapaṅktayaḥ
english: There were rows of palaces with latticed windows of ivory and silver, pleasing to behold, covered with golden nets.

sanskrit: sudhāmaṇivicitrāṇi bhūmibhāgāni sarvaśaḥ daśagrīvaḥ svabhavane prādarśayata maithilīm
english: The floors everywhere were variously decorated with plaster and gems; Daśagrīva showed all these to Maithilī in his own dwelling.

sanskrit: dīrghikāḥ puṣkariṇyaś ca nānāpuṣpasamāvṛtāḥ rāvaṇo darśayām āsa sītāṃ śokaparāyaṇām
english: Rāvaṇa showed grief-stricken Sītā the long ponds and lotus pools covered with diverse flowers.

sanskrit: darśayitvā tu vaidehīṃ kṛtsnaṃ tad bhavanottamam uvāca vākyaṃ pāpātmā rāvaṇo janakātmajām
english: Having shown Vaidehī, the daughter of Janaka, all of that magnificent dwelling, the wicked-souled Rāvaṇa spoke these words to her.

sanskrit: daśarākṣasakoṭyaś ca dvāviṃśatir athāparāḥ varjayitvā jarā vṛddhān bālāṃś ca rajanīcarān
english: "One hundred and twenty million night-wandering rākṣasas, excluding the old, the aged, and the young —

sanskrit: teṣāṃ prabhur ahaṃ sīte sarveṣāṃ bhīmakarmaṇām sahasram ekam ekasya mama kāryapuraḥsaram
english: "Of all those — terrible in deed, O Sītā — I am the lord; one thousand of them stand ready, each one, to execute my commands."

sanskrit: yad idaṃ rājyatantraṃ me tvayi sarvaṃ pratiṣṭhitam jīvitaṃ ca viśālākṣi tvaṃ me prāṇair garīyasī
english: "This entire realm and sovereignty of mine rests in you; my life too, O wide-eyed one — you are dearer to me than my own breath."

sanskrit: bahūnāṃ strīsahasrāṇāṃ mama yo 'sau parigrahaḥ tāsāṃ tvam īśvarī sīte mama bhāryā bhava priye
english: "Of the many thousands of women who are in my household, you, Sītā, shall be sovereign over them all — become my wife, my beloved."

sanskrit: sādhu kiṃ te 'nyayā buddhyā rocayasva vaco mama bhajasva mābhitaptasya prasādaṃ kartum arhasi
english: "Come, what use is this contrary mind of yours? Find my words pleasing; I am consumed with longing — you ought to bestow your grace upon me."

sanskrit: parikṣiptā samudreṇa laṅkeyaṃ śatayojanā neyaṃ dharṣayituṃ śakyā sendrair api surāsuraiḥ
english: "This Laṅkā, encircled by the ocean, spanning a hundred yojanas, cannot be assailed even by gods and asuras with Indra at their head."

sanskrit: na deveṣu na yakṣeṣu na gandharveṣu narṣiṣu ahaṃ paśyāmi lokeṣu yo me vīryasamo bhavet
english: "Neither among gods, nor yakṣas, nor gandharvas, nor among human sages — I see none in all the worlds who might equal me in valor."

sanskrit: rājyabhraṣṭena dīnena tāpasena gatāyuṣā kiṃ kariṣyasi rāmeṇa mānuṣeṇālpatejasā
english: "What will you do with Rāma — a mere mortal, wretched, bereft of his kingdom, a wandering ascetic, of little splendor, whose life is as good as gone?"

sanskrit: bhajasva sīte mām eva bhartāhaṃ sadṛśas tava yauvanaṃ hy adhruvaṃ bhīru ramasveha mayā saha
english: "Cherish me alone, O Sītā — I am a husband worthy of you; youth is impermanent, O timid one; enjoy yourself here with me."

sanskrit: darśane mā kṛthā buddhiṃ rāghavasya varānane kāsya śaktir ihāgantum api sīte manorathaiḥ
english: "Direct not your mind to the sight of Rāghava, O most beautiful-faced one; who has the power to come here, O Sītā, even in imagination?"

sanskrit: na śakyo vāyur ākāśe pāśair baddhaṃ mahājavaḥ dīpyamānasya vāpy agner grahītuṃ vimalāṃ śikhām
english: "The mighty swift wind cannot be fettered in the sky with snares, nor the pure flame of blazing fire be grasped."

sanskrit: trayāṇām api lokānāṃ na taṃ paśyāmi śobhane vikrameṇa nayed yas tvāṃ madbāhuparipālitām
english: "In all three worlds I see none, O beautiful one, who by valor could take you away from the shelter of my arms."

sanskrit: laṅkāyāṃ sumahad rājyam idaṃ tvam anupālaya abhiṣekodakaklinnā tuṣṭā ca ramayasva mām
english: "Rule with me this vast kingdom of Laṅkā; anointed with consecration waters, be content and give me delight."

sanskrit: duṣkṛtaṃ yat purā karma vanavāsena tad gatam yaś ca te sukṛto dharmas tasyeha phalam āpnuhi
english: "Whatever evil karma you have from former deeds has been expiated by your forest sojourn; now enjoy here the fruit of whatever good merit you have accumulated."

sanskrit: iha sarvāṇi mālyāni divyagandhāni maithili bhūṣaṇāni ca mukhyāni tāni seva mayā saha
english: "Here all garlands, divine fragrances, O Maithilī, and the finest ornaments — enjoy all these with me."

sanskrit: puṣpakaṃ nāma suśroṇi bhrātur vaiśravaṇasya me vimānaṃ ramaṇīyaṃ ca tad vimānaṃ manojavam
english: "There is a chariot called Puṣpaka, O beautiful-hipped one, my brother Vaiśravaṇa's; that chariot is delightful and swift as thought."

sanskrit: tatra sīte mayā sārdhaṃ viharasva yathāsukham vadanaṃ padmasaṃkāśaṃ vimalaṃ cārudarśanam
english: "In it, O Sītā, sport with me to your heart's content; your face, lotus-like, pure, lovely to behold —

sanskrit: śokārtaṃ tu varārohe na bhrājati varānane alaṃ vrīḍena vaidehi dharmalopa kṛtena te
english: "Tormented by grief, O beautiful-formed one, it does not shine, O most lovely-faced one; enough of this shame on account of the transgression of dharma ascribed to you, O Vaidehī."

sanskrit: ārṣo 'yaṃ daivaniṣyando yas tvām abhigamiṣyati etau pādau mayā snigdhau śirobhiḥ paripīḍitau
english: "This coming to you is a divine dispensation ordained by fate; these my feet, with affection, I press to my head before you."

sanskrit: prasādaṃ kuru me kṣipraṃ vaśyo dāso 'ham asmi te nemāḥ śūnyā mayā vācaḥ śuṣyamāṇena bhāṣitāḥ
english: "Grant me your favor swiftly; I am your devoted servant — let not these words spoken by me, as I wither with longing, be uttered in vain."

sanskrit: na cāpi rāvaṇaḥ kāṃ cin mūrdhnā strīṃ praṇameta ha evam uktvā daśagrīvo maithilīṃ janakātmajām
english: "Never indeed has Rāvaṇa bowed his head to any woman." Having thus spoken, Daśagrīva addressed Maithilī, the daughter of Janaka —

sanskrit: kṛtāntavaśam āpanno mameyam iti manyate
english: — thinking to himself: "She has fallen into the power of Fate; she is mine."

sanskrit: sā tathoktā tu vaidehī nirbhayā śokakarṣitā tṛṇam antarataḥ kṛtvā rāvaṇaṃ pratyabhāṣata
english: Thus addressed, Vaidehī, fearless though worn by grief, placing a blade of grass between herself and Rāvaṇa as a barrier, spoke in reply.

sanskrit: rājā daśaratho nāma dharmasetur ivācalaḥ satyasandhaḥ parijñāto yasya putraḥ sa rāghavaḥ
english: "There is a king named Daśaratha, immovable as a dyke of righteousness, known to all as true to his vows — whose son is that Rāghava."

sanskrit: rāmo nāma sa dharmātmā triṣu lokeṣu viśrutaḥ dīrghabāhur viśālākṣo daivataṃ sa patir mama
english: "He is named Rāma, righteous-souled, renowned in all three worlds, long-armed, wide-eyed — he is my god, my husband."

sanskrit: ikṣvākūṇāṃ kule jātaḥ siṃhaskandho mahādyutiḥ lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā yas te prāṇāṃ hariṣyati
english: "Born in the line of the Ikṣvākus, lion-shouldered, of great splendor — together with his brother Lakṣmaṇa, he will take your life."

sanskrit: pratyakṣaṃ yady ahaṃ tasya tvayā syāṃ dharṣitā balāt śayitā tvaṃ hataḥ saṃkhye janasthāne yathā kharaḥ
english: "Were I, who am directly his, to be violated by you by force, you would lie slain in battle just as Khara was slain at Janasthāna."

sanskrit: ya ete rākṣasāḥ proktā ghorarūpā mahābalāḥ rāghave nirviṣāḥ sarve suparṇe pannagā yathā
english: "Those rākṣasas you have described as terrible in form and mighty — before Rāghava they are all venom-less, like serpents before Garuḍa."

sanskrit: tasya jyāvipramuktās te śarāḥ kāñcanabhūṣaṇāḥ śarīraṃ vidhamiṣyanti gaṅgākūlam ivormayaḥ
english: "His arrows, adorned with gold, released from the bowstring, will tear through your body as waves batter the banks of the Gaṅgā."

sanskrit: asurair vā surair vā tvaṃ yady avadho 'si rāvaṇa utpādya sumahad vairaṃ jīvaṃs tasya na mokṣyase
english: "Even if you be invulnerable to asuras and gods, O Rāvaṇa, having provoked this great enmity, you will not escape him alive."

sanskrit: sa te jīvitaśeṣasya rāghavo 'ntakaro balī paśor yūpagatasyeva jīvitaṃ tava durlabham
english: "That mighty Rāghava will be the destroyer of what remains of your life; your survival is as uncertain as that of a sacrificial beast bound to the post."

sanskrit: yadi paśyet sa rāmas tvāṃ roṣadīptena cakṣuṣā rakṣas tvam adya nirdagdho gaccheḥ sadyaḥ parābhavam
english: "Should Rāma look upon you with eyes ablaze with fury, you would be burnt to ash that very instant, O demon, and meet immediate destruction."

sanskrit: yaś candraṃ nabhaso bhūmau pātayen nāśayeta vā sāgaraṃ śoṣayed vāpi sa sītāṃ mocayed iha
english: "He who could hurl the moon down from the sky or destroy it, who could dry up the ocean — such a one could liberate Sītā from here."

sanskrit: gatāyus tvaṃ gataśrīko gatasattvo gatendriyaḥ laṅkā vaidhavyasaṃyuktā tvatkṛtena bhaviṣyati
english: "Your life is spent, your fortune gone, your vitality gone, your senses gone; Laṅkā through your deed will be plunged into widowhood."

sanskrit: na te pāpam idaṃ karma sukhodarkaṃ bhaviṣyati yāhaṃ nītā vinā bhāvaṃ patipārśvāt tvayā vanāt
english: "This sinful act of yours — carrying me away from the forest, from my husband's side, against my will — will not yield happy results for you."

sanskrit: sa hi daivatasaṃyukto mama bhartā mahādyutiḥ nirbhayo vīryam āśritya śūnye vasati daṇḍake
english: "For my husband, of great splendor, supported by the gods, dwells fearlessly in the desolate Daṇḍaka, relying on his valor."

sanskrit: sa te darpaṃ balaṃ vīryam utsekaṃ ca tathāvidham apaneṣyati gātrebhyaḥ śaravarṣeṇa saṃyuge
english: "He will strip your pride, strength, valor, and arrogance from your limbs with a rain of arrows in battle."

sanskrit: yadā vināśo bhūtānāṃ dṛśyate kālacoditaḥ tadā kārye pramādyanti narāḥ kālavaśaṃ gatāḥ
english: "When the destruction of beings is seen, urged on by Time, then men fallen under Time's power grow heedless in their deeds."

sanskrit: māṃ pradhṛṣya sa te kālaḥ prāpto 'yaṃ rakṣasādhama ātmano rākṣasānāṃ ca vadhāyāntaḥpurasya ca
english: "By violating me, that Time has arrived for you, O vilest of demons — for the slaughter of yourself, your rākṣasas, and your inner household."

sanskrit: na śakyā yajñamadhyasthā vediḥ srugbhāṇḍa maṇḍitā dvijātimantrasaṃpūtā caṇḍālenāvamarditum
english: "An altar set in the midst of a sacrifice, adorned with ladles and vessels, consecrated by the mantras of twice-born priests, cannot be defiled by a caṇḍāla."

sanskrit: idaṃ śarīraṃ niḥsaṃjñaṃ bandha vā ghātayasva vā nedaṃ śarīraṃ rakṣyaṃ me jīvitaṃ vāpi rākṣasa na hi śakṣyāmy upakrośaṃ pṛthivyāṃ dātum ātmanaḥ
english: "This body, now insensible — bind it or slay it; I hold neither this body nor my life dear, O demon; for I cannot bring upon myself disgrace in this world."

sanskrit: evam uktvā tu vaidehī kroddhāt suparuṣaṃ vacaḥ rāvaṇaṃ maithilī tatra punar novāca kiṃ cana
english: Having thus spoken these exceedingly harsh words out of anger to Rāvaṇa, Maithilī Vaidehī said nothing further to him there.

sanskrit: sītāyā vacanaṃ śrutvā paruṣaṃ romaharṣaṇam pratyuvāca tataḥ sītāṃ bhayasaṃdarśanaṃ vacaḥ
english: Having heard Sītā's harsh, hair-raising words, he then replied to Sītā with words designed to inspire terror.

sanskrit: śṛṇu maithili madvākyaṃ māsān dvādaśa bhāmini kālenānena nābhyeṣi yadi māṃ cāruhāsini tatas tvāṃ prātarāśārthaṃ sūdāś chetsyanti leśaśaḥ
english: "Hear my words, O Maithilī, O passionate one: if within twelve months' time you do not come to me, O lovely-smiling one, the cooks will then cut you to pieces for my morning meal."

sanskrit: ity uktvā paruṣaṃ vākyaṃ rāvaṇaḥ śatrurāvaṇaḥ rākṣasīś ca tataḥ kruddha idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Having spoken these harsh words, Rāvaṇa — the terror of his enemies — then in fury spoke these words to the demonesses.

sanskrit: śīghram evaṃ hi rākṣasyo vikṛtā ghoradarśanāḥ darpam asyā vineṣyantu māṃsaśoṇitabhojanāḥ
english: "Swiftly, you demonesses of hideous and terrible appearance, eaters of flesh and blood, must break her pride."

sanskrit: vacanād eva tās tasya vikṛtā ghoradarśanāḥ kṛtaprāñjalayo bhūtvā maithilīṃ paryavārayan
english: At his mere word, those hideous and terrible demonesses, joining their palms in obeisance, surrounded Maithilī.

sanskrit: sa tāḥ provāca rājā tu rāvaṇo ghoradarśanaḥ pracālya caraṇotkarṣair dārayann iva medinīm
english: That king, Rāvaṇa of dreadful appearance, spoke to them, stamping his feet with such force it seemed to split the earth.

sanskrit: aśokavanikāmadhye maithilī nīyatām iti tatreyaṃ rakṣyatāṃ gūḍham uṣmābhiḥ parivāritā
english: "Let Maithilī be taken to the Aśoka grove; let her be guarded there in secret, surrounded by her warders."

sanskrit: tatraināṃ tarjanair ghoraiḥ punaḥ sāntvaiś ca maithilīm ānayadhvaṃ vaśaṃ sarvā vanyāṃ gajavadhūm iva
english: "There, with terrible threats and again with gentle words, bring Maithilī fully under control — as one tames a wild elephant cow."

sanskrit: iti pratisamādiṣṭā rākṣasyo rāvaṇena tāḥ aśokavanikāṃ jagmur maithilīṃ parigṛhya tām
english: Thus instructed by Rāvaṇa, those demonesses took hold of Maithilī and went to the Aśoka grove.

sanskrit: sarvakāmaphalair vṛkṣair nānāpuṣpaphalair vṛtām sarvakālamadaiś cāpi dvijaiḥ samupasevitām
english: It was surrounded by trees bearing every desired fruit, covered with diverse flowers and fruits, frequented by birds intoxicated at every season.

sanskrit: sā tu śokaparītāṅgī maithilī janakātmajā rākṣasī vaśam āpannā vyāghrīṇāṃ hariṇī yathā
english: And Maithilī, the daughter of Janaka, her limbs overcome by grief, having fallen into the power of the demonesses, was like a doe in the power of tigresses.

sanskrit: na vindate tatra tu śarma maithilī virūpanetrābhir atīva tarjitā patiṃ smarantī dayitaṃ ca devaraṃ vicetanābhūd bhayaśokapīḍitā
english: Maithilī found no comfort there, excessively threatened by those demonesses of disfigured eyes; remembering her beloved husband and dear brother-in-law, she fell into a state of unconsciousness, tormented by fear and grief.
